chapter: Porch interview and Jazz Train plans
title: Rasch on Johnson's pneumonia and the porch interview
summary: Rasch explains Johnson's illness and hospitalization and introduces a July interview on his porch.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Some of the gaps in these tapes were explained to Mr. Taylor. The date J.C. read the blues poem, was the day I won't forget -- he was lying in bed, totally drained of energy and experiencing great difficulty in breathing. I took him to the doctor for the second time on one of my visits, and he was hospitalized with what turned out to be pneumonia. He was hospitalized for approximately 8 weeks, but when he returned to Wortsboro, in July, he had made an amazing recovery.

I arranged an interview which you will now hear -- please bear with me, it was on his front porch, and if you bear with us, you will find that we come inside and he does play the piano on this tape - not much, but a little bit.
